Dec,1997   No.124   Page Reply

 How to write to us...02     -
 Harold Burton........03    04
 Cliff Jackson........05    18
 John Lunn............24     -

 Gerry Bates..........42    44
 Harold Burton........48     -
 Bernadette Dowsland..49    50

   PLEASE SEND YOUR TEXTFILE!
Text is accepted in any form for
OUTLETTERS: wordprocessor files
(say which),typed or handwritten
letters. However, PLEASE send us
a textfile if possible so your
letter needn't be typed again!
The easiest for us to edit are
Tasword 2 files with the right
margin set at 32 but a textfile
in ANY format is appreciated!

Please state if there should be
parts of your letter you do not
wish published but we always use
our discretion anyway. Letters
may also be edited for clarity
and length... Please ask if you
welcome direct correspondence
from other OUTLET readers and we
will publish your full address.

From: Harold Burton, EDINBURGH

Email:<harold.burton@which.net>


Dear Ron,

Now that I have an email address
I have noticed yours in the mag.
but you don't say anywhere that
it can be used for sending lett-
ers to the editor. Can it?

                   Harold Burton

Brian Cavers to Harold Burton

Yes, you can send any communica-
tions to us,including letters to
go in OUTLETTERS via email.

Sorry, I had not specifically
said that you can use email for
OUTLETTERS but I have just
squeezed in an extra line in our
OUTGUIDE section.

Thanks for drawing this to my
attention.

                         Brian

From: Clifford Jackson
<100572.3707@compuserve.com>

Hello Ron and Brian (again!)

Thanks for your message of 17/10
[in regard to file transfer to/
from Spectrum or SAM to PC -Ed].
I wonder if, when replying, you
could give a little more inform-
ation about your set-up as I
would expect (and prefer) that
you would wish to test the func-
tioning of the routines to be
referred to in(and possibly be
supplied with) the proposed
series before you are committed
to publication. For example; are
your Spectrums linked to Disc-
iple, Plus-D or another drive
system?


Do you use MS Windows and does
it contain Terminal? If not do
you have MS Works with its comm-
unications application?


I will happily provide, with my
compliments, cables to link a PC
to a SAM and/ or a Spectrum 128K
which uses the modified version
of a 6-pin BT telephone connect-
or if you let me know the resp-
ective cable lengths. I do not
produce cables commercially but
have supplied them to a number
of correspondents who for vari-
ous reasons did not wish to make
their own. If cables are needed
please mention the lengths and
number of pins on the PC's seri-
al port.


The software I hope to submit
will be for: PC (QBasic) SAM
Coupe with Comms Port of course.
Spectrum 128K with Disciple. I
propose to send samples of these
with brief notes (and cables if
needed), well in advance of the
final text.


I also have simple routines
which run on a 48K Spectrum with
Interface 1 and M/Drives but
have not bothered to update them
as I feel sure that the Micro-
drive version of Outlet was ab-
andoned long ago. It is possible
however that some readers may
still wish to access text files
on that medium and copies can be



supplied if you think it approp-
riate although a commented prog-
ram listing in the form of a
text file for keyboard input may
be appropriate if you feel it
worthwhile.

When I last wrote I metioned a
method I had in mind for produc-
ing text in what I thought would
be strictly 32-character format
by ensuring that each line is
terminated by the traditional
EOL bytes, CHR$ 13 and CHR$ 10.
I now realise that, while this
would faithfully reproduce
32-column text in any PC type
w/p, the physical line-length
would be increased to 34 char-
acters. That brings me to what
seems to be a contradiction as


the Outlet Guide refers to
40-character text while your
letter of 27/9 refers to 32
characters. Do those numbers
relate to the PC and Spectrum
versions respectively? If so do
you prefer 32-cols for anything
which will go in both versions?

May I respectfully suggest that
an expansion of the section of
the Guide dealing with the form-
at of text submissions may help
to clarify readers' understand-
ing of just what is required and
may produce more uniform results
in future contributions. For
example; it took me a long time
to realise that if I set the
right margin by counting char-
acters in MS Word or Works to


allow only 40 characters to dis-
play on each line, the result is
only reliable if a fixed-width
font such as Courier is chosen.


As far as I am aware this is the
only method of setting the line
length unless one is to physic-
ally press 'return' after every
32/40 characters - which seems
at odds with the principles of
modern word processing - unless
I am missing something?


I fully accept that by request-
ing that text is prepared in the
required 32/40 column mode this
does ensure that the author is



aware of the margin limitations
and is less likely to construct
tabular information which will
overflow and require much manual
editing at Outlet. However, when
that specially formatted text is
subsequently saved as ASCII(your
Guide does not refer to 'Text'
or '.txt' although all my w/ps
use those terms rather than
ASCII), the margin setting is
lost and only lines ending with
the CHR$ 13 and CHR$ 10 char-
acters will appear correctly.
All other lines, or even whole
paragraphs, will expand to the
full width of the 'window' in
which they are displayed and, in
MS Notepad, will overflow off-
screen unless 'word-wrap' is
'ON'.


While you referred to this type
of text as '80-column' in your
letter of 27/9, it can be very
much more - depending on screen
display, font size and w/p sett-
ings - if my understanding is
correct.

No doubt your conversion soft-
ware can cope with that aspect
but I am sure that I am not the
only subscriber who would wel-
come a little more information
on exactly what is required and,
more importantly, how it can
best be achieved.

I do however fully accept your
point about avoiding the use of
TABs - a topic I have preached
in connection with text prepared


in the Amstrad NC100 Notepad and
intended for transfer to SAM
Coupe using my STU program. In
my own defence I would say that
the file which caused such dis-
pleasure was hastily assembled
by combining text from several
sources and it was intended
merely for viewing in a convent-
ional word processor - at that
stage. I should have said so of
course.

I would also be grateful if you
could let me know if the Spectr-
um version of Outlet has featur-
ed a fast (m/code) freeware
routine for converting Tasword
2's 64-column text to PC format.
One of my Spectrum routines
contains BASIC conversions with


options to retain line length
(at 64-cols or any lower figure
used) or abandon line-length to
give fully re-formattable text.
The latter is of course usually
required if the text is to be
edited in a PC w/p where re-arr-
angement would be very likely.

A further option is for any non-
ASCII characters to be filtered
out - as well as those 'padding'
spaces of course. This routine
was originally written as part
of SAM TRANSFER UTILITY where it
was adequate for smallish docu-
ments but, when the capacity of
STU was increased to handle very
large files,the BASIC conversion
routines were not satisfactory
and were replaced by m/code.


When those BASIC conversion
lines were recently converted to
run on the Spectrum where funct-
ions such as INSTR aren't avail-
able, the result is pathetically
slow.

If your Spectrum readers could
be referred to an alternative
conversion routine running at a
realistic speed then the conver-
sion and transfer of significant
numbers of files from Spectrum
to PC becomes much more realist-
ic. Alternatively I must find
time to write some fresh code.

I must leave you to make any
editorial changes necessary in
the final text for the Spectrum
edition but it would be helpful


if you could give me a guide on
how the SAM or Spectrum software
could be handled in the PC vers-
ion. If you prefer to merely in-
vite readers to send me a floppy
and sae for any SAM or Spectrum
software then that is OK by me.
Would it also be desirable to
add to the Outlet disc a file
containing a 'text' listing (OCR
scanned) which could be helpful
to those readers unable not make
use of SAM or Disciple discs eg,
users of Opus,Amiga or even Z88.

Another thought is whether I can
refer to 'Press key 'X' now' to
see an image on screen should
that prove appropriate. I cannot
remember whether this is used in
Outlet or if I saw it elsewhere.


Finally, could you please indi-
cate a preferred length in bytes
or lines (max/min) for each
monthly installment.

Sorry to have droned on at such
length.

        Yours sincerely,

              Cliff Jackson


Brian Cavers to Cliff Jackson

My Spectrum setup is a 48K with
+D so it does not have a serial
port. My +3 does - but it would
defeat the object to have to
port stuff from my main 48K
system to the +3 before porting
it to the PC. My SAM is a 512K.
I am rather out of touch with
SAM and never used it for comms.
As far as I can see there is no
built-in serial port unless it
is part of the MIDI in/out sock-
ets. I do have WINDOWS 3.1 with
TERMINAL.

Thank you for your offer to sup-
ply a cable. If you think my SAM
is suitable, a cable of about 6
foot ought to be adequate.


Any reasonably short Spectrum or
SAM BASIC listing might be incl-
uded In the PC version of OUTLET
within the text of the article
or as a text file to accompany
it. The article will run simult-
aneously in the Spectrum version
and there both the original Sp-
ectrum and SAM BASIC files can
be included on the +D version to
accompany the article.


Yes, I asked for 32 column text
because that is what we use on
the Spectrum and it is far eas-
ier to expand to 40 column for
the PC - possibly leaving any
tables etc in 32 column - than
trying to reduce from 40 to 32.



The line length always refers to
the actual text length NOT inc-
luding any line feed or carriage
return codes at the end. I have
made a note to look at OUTGUIDE
regarding clarifying how text
might be submitted.

I must stress that we don't have
rules set in tablets of stone:
WE ACCEPT ANY TYPE OF TEXT FILE
IN ANY FORMAT!We only let people
know the format that saves us a
lot of unnecessary labour. There
are scores of DOS text editors
and word processors that produce
standard ASCII text that will
work on ANY system and ANY comp-
uter- it's these newer WINDOWS
based wordprocessors that have
their own standards which only
work on their own WP!

I have not been able to find a
fast Tasword 2 to ASCII text
format convertor but the easiest
way might be to write it in
QUICK BASIC and convert it AFTER
it has transferred to PC?

The largest single text file in
our own Spectrum compress file
format is about 55 to 60 screen
pages of 22 lines of 32 char-
acters which is about 38K in its
original uncompressed format.
However, I recommend you aim at
half or less than that for each
article - say, 3000 words?

Image files with sketch diagrams
etc can be included but again,
these use memory.On the Spectrum
we compress these from 7K down


to maybe 2 or 3K depending on
the complexity and this has to
steal memory from the text so
allow for that in the text
length.No more than two or three
images per article is normal.

On the PC the images use a rela-
tively similar proportion and I
can convert from Spectrum to PC
(more difficult the other way!)

If you simply put a message in
the text where you want an image
to be I will edit it
appropriately. Typically I say
something like...

PRESS GRAPHICS KEY TO SEE SCREEN
on the Spectrum and on the PC...
SELECT eXtra BUTTON...


On either system these are norm-
ally linked to the text Page
number so it is easier if there
is only one image on any one
page.

REMEMBER THAT ALL TEXT GETS ED-
ITED BY ME FOR VARIOUS REASONS
INCLUDING SPACING, HOUSE STYLE,
GRAMMAR, SYNTAX, SPELLING, PAGE
FORMATTING, ETC! BUT I DO STRIVE
TO LEAVE IT AS CLOSE AS INTENDED
BY THE AUTHOR!

Well, I hope I have not missed
anything out but let me know
next time if so.

                          Brian

From: John Lunn, BOLTON

Dear Ron & Brian,

I'll start by prematurely wish-
ing you and all the readers a
Merry Christmas and a Good 98.

Regarding feedback on the future
of the Spectrum version of Out-
let, I would like to comment the
following way. I appreciate
Outlet is a hobby rather than a
business, but it must not make a
loss. A bespoke business offers
quality rather than quantity,
whereas the quantity at cheap
price philosophy, in the main,
makes the "QUICK BUCK" but is
not around for very long. I
would therefore advocate for the
bi-monthly option.  - John Lunn

From: Gerry Bates, SHEFFIELD
<gerrybates@compuserve.com>

Dear Brian & Ron,

With regard to recent correspon-
dence on transferring text files
from Spectrum and SAM to PC;
there is a software solution for
the latter. "PC Suite" from S.D.
Software enables the SAM not
only to write to a PC disk but
format a 720k PC disk itself. I
submitted my own routine to "SAM
Supplement" to enable a SAM to
read "Tasword II" files from an
Opus Discovery disk, so anyone
with all three machines could
use this software solution to
transfer from Spectrum to PC al-
beit in two stages.


It shouldn't be impossible for
the PC to read Spectrum disks
directly -maybe I'll put my mind
to it when I've finished off the
bathroom,rebuilt the MG,finished
off the loft conversion, built
the model railway...

Incidentally, "Tasword II" files
are pure text so there should be
no problem in importing them
into any PC word processor.

             Regards,

              Gerry Bates

Brian Cavers to Gerry Bates

Thanks, Gerry.

There is a utility that comes
with the registered version of
the Lunter Z80 Spectrum emulator
that permits Plus D or Disciples
to be read by a PC and I use
this a lot for transferring text
files and sometimes images from
the Spectrum.

See also the OUTLETTER from
Cliff Jackson.

                     Brian


           COLIN BIBBY
         2 MOORCROFT RD
          NORTHERN MOOR
           WYTHENSHAWE
           MANCHESTER
             M23 0WJ






Dear Outlet readers,
(Mr Perry & Tony Ward
particularly),

Many thanks for your support and
chats. Has there ever been such
a brill zine as Outlet before? I
DOUBT IT. Keep up the good work
lads and lasses. LUV IT!


Many thanks also to Malcolm (Mr
Perry) who is obviously well and
truly a fellow ZXer. My delayed
replies here aren't of snobbery
Malcolm. A couple of downstairs
rooms have been receiving some-
thing of an uplift during the
last month or so to the decor.
It's plain hell here at present
all taking much longer than
anticipated largely due to a
scumbag who recently robbed my
parents while they were both at
home. Might give all that a men-
tion at the end of this letter.


Apologies to all who continue to
struggle with the 3.5" drive
data ribbon & psu leads for the
+3 "B" drive.Be patient.It pays.


I'm sure Malcolm will agree that
there are a few too many reasons
(for why your own 3.5" drive is
refusing to function) to list
here. As stated, BE PATIENT.

I personally think you will have
made good of the leads you made
up Tony. Its a reasonably
straightforward job whether you
are a technical wizard or not.
You will no doubt have already
tried the data lead upside down.
NO HARM DONE TRYING IT THAT WAY.
The only fuses blown are in your
head when all else fails.

You say the drive is known to
be a good one Tony and it may be
so. Oh boy, this is such a big
subject that the best advice I
can offer is TRY ANOTHER drive.

I think Malcolm might be writing
you some further details since
reading your letter.


In brief:-

A few jumpers or dip switches at
the rear of your drive might
need some twiddling with. That's
probably why you are getting the
error messages.

Your drive might not even have
such jumpers fitted. Some drives
have been manufactured minus the
switches etc -probably to reduce
costs. In such cases the drive
will have been factory preset
via short wiring of the pcb for
a particular pc/mode I think?


BIG SUBJECT. Malcolm Perry is
your man Tony, having far more
knowledge than myself on all
this. However, if you are keen
to send me your drive and/or
leads plus return p&p etc for
checking out, my address is at
the top of this letter.


PLEASE NOTE: I DO NOT AND CANNOT
TAKE ON SUCH PROJECTs AS A
REGULAR PROFESSION. BUT I WILL
CERTAINLY DO MY BEST TO TEST AND
VERIFY READY MADE LEADs THEN
INSTRUCT AS NESCESSARY. THIS CAN
NOT INCLUDE ANY NECESSARY ALTER-
ATIONs - ADJUSTMENTs - REPAIRs
WHICH WOULD NEED TO BE CARRIED
OUT LATER BY YOURSELF.

.

YOUR DRIVE LEADs,IF CORRECT,WILL
OPERATE PERFECTLY WITH MY OWN
DRIVES THEREFORE PROVING YOUR
DRIVE ONLY TO BE THE PROBLEM.

NO GUARANTEES0,NOR WILL I ACCEPT
ANY RESPONSIBILITY FOR ITEMS
LOST OR DAMAGED IN TRANSIT OR
OTHERWISE. (NO CONMEN THANKS,
PLEASE). ALLOW A WEEK OR SO. DO
REMEMBER - IT'S XMASTIME. SEND
AN SAE... NO SAE = NO REPLY.

Back to the robbery. It was on a
Thursday in November- Mum's 81st
birthday. Mother had just nipped
out to the corner shop returning
slowly (as she does these days)
with purse in hand. She entered
the lower level security doors
then into the lift followed by a
well-dressed smart guy.

Hearing problems rife, she asked
his floor then pressed the nec-
essary buttons in the lift for
both he and she.

As the lift reached mum's floor
this guy proceeded to follow.
Mum said "yours is the next one"
then continued on her way to her
flat not realising he had foll-
owed at a slight distance.

Still with purse in hand she
opened the door then was pushed
aside as the robber forced his
way past and into the living
room where pop(aged 88) was sat.
Dad instantly thought this guy
was a rep or likewise as he
strolled gradually round BROUGHT
IN BY MUM.


To cut a longer story short:-
Neither were hurt THANKFULLY. He
got away with mum's purse only
which contained around `30 and
no keys etc.My eyes filling as I
write here are probably doing so
from frustration more than any-
thing else. I CAN'T FIND THE B!


I have since invested in one of
the CCT video cameras from
Maplin. For those curious, these
are available from around `64 +
vat for a mono (b/w) version
though the one I opted for was
`99 incl and slightly smaller.
In fact it would fit into a
space smaller than a matchbox.
The `64 model on the other hand
is about the size of a matchbox.


These (pcbs only) have three
only wiring connections to make
being the GND (Ground - Neg).
POS (Positive 12v regulated psu)
therefor will also 12v car batt
operate if suited. Signal(direct
to video scart or via modulator
(`30) to tv).

Maplin staff are a very helpful
crew. Our `99 CCT camera will be
fitted and concealed within a
Maplin intercom box then wall
mounted outside my parents'front
door this weekend for both sound
and visual scans. IT'S A GREAT
XMAS PRESSY AND NEW TOY FOR POP!

      BEST WISHES TO ALL!

             COLIN

From Chris Oliver, STAFFS



Regarding your problem with the
update to PROCROSS detailed in
your letter in Issue #122...

It is possible that the problem
stems from the ROM keyboard
reading routine. I notice that
your KEYUSR reads the value in
system variable LAST_K at 23560,
and seem to remember having
difficuties in the distant past
when doing the same, but cannot
remember the details.

The ROM keyboard scanning and
interpretation routines are vast
and complex, but can be a little


'dim' and easily confused. If
for instance in "K" mode you
hold down key "D", you get "DIM
DIM DIM DIM DIM ....." on the
screen! If however, you press
key "D" then let it up for a
moment before holding it down,
you will see "DIM ddddddd....."
as you would expect.

My suspicions seemed to be
confirmed when I did a test on
the KEYUSR demo in OUTLET 110.
I typed in nonsense very fast,
keeping my fingers well away
from the BREAK and SHIFT keys,
and on at least five occasions a
soft crash occurred, giving the
error report "L BREAK in program
1000 : 1". I stress 'WITHOUT
touching BREAK or SHIFT keys'!


CONCLUSION:-
There is possibly a bug in the
Spectrun ROM keyboard routine?

SOLUTION:-
Simply write your own keyboard
scanning routine!

Simply?? Well after about a day
and a half bimbling about in the
ROM with the assistance of Logan
and O'Hara's ROM DISSASEMBLY and
Francis Miles' ROM INDEX, a
working routine emerged which
uses just a few calls to parts
of the ROM.

The machine code routine is
quite short and will be easily
understood by yourself, but for
the benefit of anyone not so


experienced in machine code, I
have explained each step in
detail in the OUTCLASS in this
issue.
                        Chris

Brian Cavers to Chris Oliver

Many thanks, Chris.

Malcolm Goodman has also given
me a lot of help and ideas and I
plan to give the whole keyboard
routine a complete overhaul as
soon as I can find the time.

                    Brian

From: Gerry Bates

Following Bernadette Dowsland's
Outletter in Spectrum Issue
No.123; you asked for comments
on the future of the Spectrum
version of Outlet.

I am a relative newcomer - foll-
owing the demise of the Spectrum
Discovery Club - so I probably
haven't had time to notice the
things about which Bernadette
complains. It's still quite new
and exciting to me and I'm quite
glad that someone out there
still takes an interest in the
Spectrum. I very gratefully acc-
epted a free sample of PC Outlet
which arrived at about the same
time as No.123 and I read it
first.

Being sufficiently impressed I
printed out the order form on
the disk and sent it off with my
cheque. But did I do the right
thing?

When I came to look at the Spec-
trum issue I found that a lot of
it was common to the PC version,
down to the least relevant incl-
usion, "The Girl from Ipanema"!
Is this a symptom of not having
enough relevant PC material to
fill the PC Outlet either?
Perhaps, as well as falling back
to bi-monthly, the two versions
should be combined, ie the same
contents available on either
Spectrum or PC format disks!

                 Gerry Bates

Brian Cavers to Gerry Bates




Thanks for your comments, Gerry.
I was a bit shocked to read two
things though: First...

"a LOT was common [to both Spec-
trum and PC version of OUTLET]".

I went hurrying back to the last
issue to see. Apart from some
readers' letters which were
clearly relevant to both PC and
Spectrum users (LIKE YOUR LETTER
AND THIS REPLY!) the ONLY item
common to both issues was the
article you mentioned:"The Girl
From Ipanema".


I've never checked exactly but
after expansion, OUTLET must be
2 to 3 megabytes of material on
the PC, ie, say 2,500,000 bytes
roughly. "Ipanema" is about 4500
of that, ie 0.2% !!!!!!!!!


If I had left out"Ipanema" then
it would only have left around
4K spare. What else could I have
put in? Incidentally,the article
was contributed by a PC reader
for the PC version and ported
over to the Spectrum - not the
other way round - and because it
is of general interest to almost
anyone.


This leads to the second point..


You referred to "Ipanema" as
"the least relevant" and as not
having enough "relevant" materi-
al. This is based on a misunder-
standing that OUTLET is limited
to only computer-related items I
think. Not so; we welcome short
stories and other articles (this
is the PURPOSE of OUTPUT)-almost
anything publishable - witness
the many SHOUTBURSTS and other
articles over the years on a
wide range of topics.

OUTLET is YOUR magazine; it's
what the readers want to make
it. We can only publish what is
sent in to us plus add any publ-
ic domain material.If we started
to get inundated with OUTLETTERS
on say, printers(incidentally of


common interest to both PC and
Spectrum users) then that would
dominate even if some readers
were not interested.

There will always be some mater-
ial that is of interest to some
and not others. Surely it is
fair to include items even if
only one reader in a hundred
might enjoy it - especially if
they only use a trivial amount
of disk space?

However, your comments are list-
ened to with interest(well I did
ask for them didn't I!) so write
again.

                       Brian

From: Bernadette Dowsland, GOOLE

Dear Ron,

Why not bring out a compilation
disc of PROCROSS together with
all the data files so far pub-
lished in your magazine? I prod-
uced such a disc last evening.
It looked pretty impressive and
that's bearing in mind I don't
have a complete collection of
OUTLET.

So, how about it? Does it seem a

more than a few hours to do.

          Bernadette

Good idea! Mind you, I'm working

until that is ready.

                         Brian.

From: Harold Burton, EDINBURGH

Email:<harold.burton@which.net>

Dear Ron,

Now that I have an email address I have noticed yours in the mag. but you don't say anywhere that it can be used for sending lett- ers to the editor. Can it?

Harold Burton
